summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis was admitted for an acute flare characterized by severe abdominal pain unresponsive to oral Dilaudid. She was managed with IV pain control, transitioned back to oral opioids, and started on gabapentin for neuropathic pain. The fentanyl patch was increased to 100 mcg every 72 hours. TPN was continued for malnutrition. A CT scan showed no evidence of acute or chronic pancreatitis or complications but revealed borderline mediastinal lymph nodes requiring follow-up chest CT. Iron deficiency anemia was diagnosed based on low ferritin, and oral iron was initiated with plans for outpatient colonoscopy. Blood cultures and chest imaging showed no infection. Pain improved, and she was discharged home with stable condition, afebrile, on TPN, and with updated medications including iron, gabapentin, and a stronger fentanyl patch.
